visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md (locked 2026-08-11). There is no index.html in this directory. The visual target is the six closed patterns in PUBLIC_UI.md, built from components/site/v3.
note: Homes grain fix 2026-08-14. Rhythm: THREE of the six patterns, no two adjacent alike, chrome exempt. Order is Breadcrumb, Field of the cut houses as a V3Carousel photo rail (count is a caption, never an Instrument hero), Drawing of the week's cuts, Sheet, Quiet, Footer. The empty window substitutes a Quiet for the Field and is still three patterns. Every figure comes from ONE getPriceDrops({ limit: 48, days: 7 }) call. Absent is not zero: an empty resilient-cache fallback is opted out of ISR with noStore(), and Dataset / updated / count figures are omitted rather than published as 0. Drop math is previous list price to current list price. Field rows sort by lastDropPct descending. HideAwareListingGrid is a declared deletion: hidden-home subtraction stays on /search. SITE-70: photographs open via shadcn-carousel -> V3Carousel; ItemList JSON-LD lists the cut homes.
deletions: KbHero: the dark photo hero and its live-glance counts. The counts survive as Instrument figures when the pull is non-empty.
KbFeatured: the poster grid of the biggest percent reductions. Those homes are Field rows now, sorted by lastDropPct descending.
KbListingMap: replaced by the Field's built-in plot of rows that carry coordinates.

HideAwareListingGrid: the per-user hidden-aware ListingCard grid (W7.2). Hidden-home subtraction stays on /search. This page is a curated 7-day cut list, not a browse of for-sale inventory, and it does not import a raw listing renderer.
Neighborhood mini-table: the 7-day pull grouped by subdivision. Field row meta still names displaySubdivision when the feed has a readable name.
City chip sections: the filter-nav and every-city chip rows. City doors live in the closing Quiet.
KbCommunityAlerts markup: replaced by PriceDropAlertsSheet on V3Sheet. Capture contract unchanged (see dataLayer), including the company honeypot.
KbSell: the seller band. Seller ask lives on Sell. The house is the primary on this buyer Field.
CTABar: the closing talk-to-a-broker bar. Not carried.
V3Instrument number hero: 60 / $3.2M / 5.6% and the method essay. Count is a caption beside the Field.
DisplayHeading / PageBreadcrumb hidden parity hacks on the city route.
SmoothScrollProvider: the Lenis wrapper. The v3 register does not hijack scroll.
KbFooter and KbBreadcrumb: replaced by V3Footer and V3Breadcrumb.

sectionOrder: PriceDropsOpening -- the H1 and the count of homes that cut price
V3Field #cuts -- V3Carousel rail of photographed cut houses (price, address, beds/baths/sqft)
V3Drawing #spread -- distribution of this week's cuts (after photographs)
V3SourceLine -- the trace and the stamp under the set
PriceDropAlertsSheet -- the ask: tell me when a home cuts price
competitiveTarget: Beat Zillow's and Redfin's price-cut filters on a page a search engine can actually rank. Their reductions live behind a filter state with no indexable URL; this is a standing page for 'price reductions bend oregon' and 'price drops central oregon' that publishes the cut homes themselves, each one a door, with the source trace and the refresh stamp under the set. The answer -- how many homes cut price and by how much -- is in text, not only in the list.

tasteReview.evaluator: separate grok-4.6 via npx tsx scripts/taste-evaluate.ts price-drops --url http://127.0.0.1:3270/price-drops --beat 30. Builder is grok-4.5 and did not grade its own page. First-viewport instrument at 1440×900 and 375×812; three scorings of one capture; median.

shotSpec.capture: scripts/take-route-shots.mjs first viewport from lane dev server :3270

tasteReview.beats: Redfin price-reduced search — this page wins on a standing URL and a beeswarm of the week's cut sizes; it loses the card, where Redfin's drop amount is a first-class mark and this rail is still photo-plus-badge. Better than a 30/100 page because photographs open, the count is a caption, listing facts sit on the card, and the drawing exists.
tasteReview.dullest: Previous/Next outline buttons under the rail — not the shadcn carousel chevron chrome a visitor would recognize from the demo.
tasteReview.verdict: Better than a 30: the fold opens on photographed cuts with the count as a caption, cards carry price/was/beds/baths/sqft, and the beeswarm is a real drawing of the week. SEO rose via title and ItemList JSON-LD. Remaining: portal-card look, text Previous/Next vs shadcn chevrons, clipped drawing in the first viewport, new-listings ask.

defects.finding: The opening is a portal listing carousel, not a field of cut houses: each cell is photo, percent badge, price, was-line, address, specs. The 3px stroke under the ask reads as a price underline — drop percents do not compare across houses as a first-class mark.
Previous and Next are outlined text buttons parked under the track. The shadcn carousel demo is chevron icon buttons on the rail you drag; a visitor would not recognize the same control.
Photographs exist, but they do not read as a field. Five vertical listing cards with full bodies dominate the first viewport; the houses are inventory tiles, not a field of cuts.
On /price-drops the visible ask is Get new Central Oregon listings by email. The conversion path is for new listings, not cuts, so the page job and the form job disagree. Product contract held.
At 1440 the first viewport clips the drawing to a few unlabeled dots with no axis and no reading, so the differentiator arrives as leftover marks under the rail.

tasteReview.rebaselineReason: evaluatorModel (claude-sonnet-5 → grok-4.6), rubricVersion (v1-2026-09-08 → v1-2026-09-10), and shotsHash all differ from the prior SITE-49 receipt; first grok-4.6 mark on rubric v1-2026-09-10 for this route.
